items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: Phil Craig told me that he, he had a good way up with very young children.

ctx.x: I think it's important to mention things. People like, uh, Johnny, I mean, who, who, who could give us even a secondhand account of Johnny's high school days of being rather mischievous? Which, you know, I could certainly see. I thought Johnny was fantastically nice to us, and, uh, uh, very helpful in helping us listen to things. Well, you know, considering that Johnny spent so many years

teaching in the, in the high schools, I imagine he either had a certain, he would have either developed a certain amount of tolerance or total intolerance. I suspect tolerance is what he developed. Although he certainly wasn't the most patient man around in some ways. Well, Phil Craig told me that he, he had a good way up with very young children. I'm making little jokes like

we're, we're going to be here at two, two, two, just like a train, or something, some sort of jokes he was making. The young, the very young boys, which he taught. I guess what, I forget what Bill was faking, he's laid out drunk. I think maybe drunk, but anyway. Uh, they, they, everyone seemed to speak highly of Johnny's pupils and everything, and he sure was kind. I think we learned a lot, cause he, I never knew which Johnny Wigs I was going to meet, depending on his mood.
